verses.zh: 你们要称谢耶和华，求告他的名，在万民中传扬他的作为！
verses.en: Give thanks to the Lord.Call on his name.Make known his accomplishments among the nations.

verses.zh: 要向他唱诗歌颂，谈论他一切奇妙的作为！
verses.en: Sing to him.Make music to him.Tell about all his miraculous deeds.

verses.zh: 要以他的圣名夸耀！寻求耶和华的人，心中应当欢喜！
verses.en: Boast about his holy name.Let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice.

verses.zh: 要寻求耶和华与他的能力，时常寻求他的面。
verses.en: Seek the Lord and the strength he gives.Seek his presence continually.

verses.zh: 他仆人亚伯拉罕的后裔，他所拣选雅各的子孙哪，你们要记念他奇妙的作为和他的奇事，并他口中的判语。
verses.en: Recall the miraculous deeds he performed,his mighty acts and the judgments he decreed,[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 105. The psalmist summons Israel to praise God because he delivered his people from Egypt in fulfillment of his covenantal promises to Abraham. A parallel version of vv. 1-15 appears in 1 Chr 16:8-22.

verses.zh: a
verses.en: O children[NOTE:1] of Abraham,[NOTE:2] God’s[NOTE:3] servant,you descendants[NOTE:4] of Jacob, God’s[NOTE:5] chosen ones.
notes: Heb “and the judgments of his mouth.”
Or “offspring”; Heb “seed.”
Some mss have “Israel,” which appears in the parallel version of this psalm in 1 Chr 16:13.
Heb “his”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “sons.”

verses.zh: 他是耶和华―我们的　神；全地都有他的判断。
verses.en: He is the Lord our God;he carries out judgment throughout the earth.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他记念他的约，直到永远；他所吩咐的话，直到千代―
verses.en: He always remembers his covenantal decree,the promise he made[NOTE:1] to a thousand generations—
notes: Heb “in all the earth [are] his judgments.”

verses.zh: 就是与亚伯拉罕所立的约，向以撒所起的誓。
verses.en: the promise[NOTE:1] he made to Abraham,the promise he made by oath to Isaac.
notes: Heb “[the] word he commanded.” The text refers here to God’s unconditional covenantal promise to Abraham and the patriarchs, as vv. 10-12 make clear.

verses.zh: 他又将这约向雅各定为律例，向以色列定为永远的约，
verses.en: He gave it to Jacob as a decree,to Israel as a lasting promise,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “which.”

verses.zh: 说：我必将迦南地赐给你，作你产业的分。
verses.en: saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaanas the portion of your inheritance.”

verses.zh: 当时，他们人丁有限，数目稀少，并且在那地为寄居的。
verses.en: When they were few in number,just a very few, and resident foreigners within it,

verses.zh: 他们从这邦游到那邦，从这国行到那国。
verses.en: they wandered from nation to nation,and from one kingdom to another.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “eternal covenant.”

verses.zh: 他不容甚么人欺负他们，为他们的缘故责备君王，
verses.en: He let no one oppress them;he disciplined kings for their sake,

verses.zh: 说：不可难为我受膏的人，也不可恶待我的先知。
verses.en: saying,[NOTE:1] “Don’t touch my chosen ones.[NOTE:2]Don’t harm my prophets.”
notes: Heb “and from a kingdom to another nation.”
The word “saying” is supplied in the translation for clarification and for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 他命饥荒降在那地上，将所倚靠的粮食全行断绝，
verses.en: He called down a famine upon the earth;he cut off all the food supply.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “anointed.”

verses.zh: 在他们以先打发一个人去―约瑟被卖为奴仆。
verses.en: He sent a man ahead of them[NOTE:1]—Joseph was sold as a servant.
notes: Heb “and every staff of food he broke.” The psalmist refers to the famine that occurred in Joseph’s time (see v. 17 and Gen 41:53-57).

verses.zh: 人用脚镣伤他的脚；他被铁链捆拘。
verses.en: The shackles hurt his feet;[NOTE:1] his neck was placed in an iron collar,[NOTE:2]
notes: After the reference to the famine in v. 16, v. 17 flashes back to events that preceded the famine (see Gen 37).
Heb “they afflicted his feet with shackles.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的话试炼他，直等到他所说的应验了。
verses.en: until the time when his prediction[NOTE:1] came true.The Lord’s word[NOTE:2] proved him right.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his neck came [into] iron.” The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) with the suffix could mean simply “he” or “his life.” But the nuance “neck” makes good sense here (note the reference to his “feet” in the preceding line). See L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 38.
Heb “word,” probably referring to Joseph’s prediction about the fate of Pharaoh’s cupbearer and baker (see Gen 41:9-14).

This line may refer to Joseph’s prediction of the famine in response to Pharaoh’s dream. Joseph emphasized to Pharaoh that the interpretation of the dream came from God (see Gen 41:16, 25, 28, 32, 39).

verses.zh: 王打发人把他解开，就是治理众民的，把他释放，
verses.en: The king authorized his release;[NOTE:1] the ruler of nations set him free.
notes: Heb “refined him.”

verses.zh: 立他作王家之主，掌管他一切所有的，
verses.en: He put him in charge of his palace,[NOTE:1] and made him manager of all his property,
notes: Heb “[the] king sent and set him free.”

verses.zh: 使他随意捆绑他的臣宰，将智慧教导他的长老。
verses.en: giving him authority to imprison his officials[NOTE:1] and to teach his advisers.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he made him master of his house.”
Heb “to bind his officials by his will.”

verses.zh: 以色列也到了埃及；雅各在含地寄居。
verses.en: Israel moved to[NOTE:1] Egypt;Jacob lived for a time[NOTE:2] in the land of Ham.
notes: Heb “and his elders he taught wisdom.”
Heb “entered.”

verses.zh: 耶和华使他的百姓生养众多，使他们比敌人强盛，
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] made his people very fruitfuland made them[NOTE:2] more numerous than their[NOTE:3] enemies.
notes: Heb “lived as a resident foreigner.”
Heb “and he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “him,” referring to “his people.”

verses.zh: 使敌人的心转去恨他的百姓，并用诡计待他的仆人。
verses.en: He caused the Egyptians[NOTE:1] to hate his peopleand to mistreat[NOTE:2] his servants.
notes: Heb “his,” referring to “his people.”
Heb “their heart.”

verses.zh: 他打发他的仆人摩西和他所拣选的亚伦，
verses.en: He sent his servant Moses,and Aaron, whom he had chosen.

verses.zh: 在敌人中间显他的神迹，在含地显他的奇事。
verses.en: They executed his miraculous signs among them[NOTE:1] and his amazing deeds in the land of Ham.
notes: Or “to deal deceptively.” The Hitpael of נָכַל (nakhal) occurs only here and in Gen 37:18, where it is used of Joseph’s brothers “plotting” to kill him.

verses.zh: 他命黑暗，就有黑暗；没有违背他话的。
verses.en: He made it dark;[NOTE:1] Moses and Aaron did not disobey his orders.[NOTE:2]
notes: Apparently the pronoun refers to “his servants” (i.e., the Israelites, see v. 25).
He made it dark. The psalmist begins with the ninth plague (see Exod 10:21-29).tn Heb “he sent darkness and made it dark.”

verses.zh: 他叫埃及的水变为血，叫他们的鱼死了。
verses.en: He turned the Egyptians’ water into bloodand killed their fish.

verses.zh: 在他们的地上以及王宫的内室，青蛙多多滋生。
verses.en: Their land was overrun by frogs,which even got into the rooms of their kings.

verses.zh: 他说一声，苍蝇就成群而来，并有虱子进入他们四境。
verses.en: He ordered flies to come;[NOTE:1] gnats invaded their whole territory.
notes: Heb “they did not rebel against his words.” Apparently this refers to Moses and Aaron, who obediently carried out God’s orders.

verses.zh: 他给他们降下冰雹为雨，在他们的地上降下火焰。
verses.en: He sent hail along with the rain;[NOTE:1] there was lightning in their land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he spoke and flies came.”
Heb “he gave their rains hail.”

verses.zh: 他也击打他们的葡萄树和无花果树，毁坏他们境内的树木。
verses.en: He destroyed their vines and fig treesand broke the trees throughout their territory.

verses.zh: 他说一声，就有蝗虫蚂蚱上来，不计其数，
verses.en: He ordered locusts to come,[NOTE:1] innumerable grasshoppers.
notes: Heb “fire of flames [was] in their land.”

verses.zh: 吃尽了他们地上各样的菜蔬和田地的出产。
verses.en: They ate all the vegetation in their landand devoured the crops of their fields.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he spoke and locusts came.”

verses.zh: 他又击杀他们国内一切的长子，就是他们强壮时头生的。
verses.en: He struck down all the firstborn in their land,the firstfruits of their reproductive power.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the fruit of their ground.”

verses.zh: 他领自己的百姓带银子金子出来；他支派中没有一个软弱的。
verses.en: He brought his people[NOTE:1] out enriched[NOTE:2] with silver and gold;none of his tribes stumbled.
notes: Verses 28-36 recall the plagues in a different order than the one presented in Exodus: v. 28 (plague 9), v. 29 (plague 1), v. 30 (plague 2), v. 31a (plague 4), v. 31b (plague 3), vv. 32-33 (plague 7), vv. 34-35 (plague 8), v. 36 (plague 10). No reference is made in Ps 105 to plagues 5 and 6.tn Heb “the beginning of all their strength,” that is, reproductive power (see Ps 78:51).
Heb “them”; the referent (the Lord’s people) has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他们出来的时候，埃及人便欢喜；原来埃及人惧怕他们。
verses.en: Egypt was happy when they left,for they were afraid of them.[NOTE:1]
notes: The word “enriched” is supplied in the translation for clarification and for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 他铺张云彩当遮盖，夜间使火光照。
verses.en: He spread out a cloud for a cover,[NOTE:1] and provided a fire to light up the night.
notes: Heb “for fear of them had fallen upon them.”

verses.zh: 他们一求，他就使鹌鹑飞来，并用天上的粮食叫他们饱足。
verses.en: They asked for food,[NOTE:1] and he sent quail;he satisfied them with food from the sky.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “curtain.”

Heb “he [i.e., his people] asked.” The singular form should probably be emended to a plural שָׁאֲלוּ (shaʾalu, “they asked”), the ו (vav) having fallen off by haplography (note the vav at the beginning of the following form).

verses.zh: 他打开磐石，水就涌出；在干旱之处，水流成河。
verses.en: He opened up a rock and water flowed out;a river ran through dry regions.

verses.zh: 这都因他记念他的圣言和他的仆人亚伯拉罕。
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] he remembered the sacred promise[NOTE:2] he made to Abraham his servant.
notes: Or “bread of heaven.” The reference is to manna (see Exod 16:4, 13-15).
Or “for.”

verses.zh: 他带领百姓欢乐而出，带领选民欢呼前往。
verses.en: When he led his people out, they rejoiced;his chosen ones shouted with joy.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his holy word.”

verses.zh: 他将列国的地赐给他们，他们便承受众民劳碌得来的，
verses.en: He handed the territory of nations over to them,and they took possession of what other peoples had produced,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he led his people out with joy, with a ringing cry, his chosen ones.”

verses.zh: 好使他们遵他的律例，守他的律法。你们要赞美耶和华！
verses.en: so that they might keep his commandsand obey[NOTE:1] his laws.Praise the Lord.
notes: Heb “and the [product of the] work of peoples they possessed.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT
PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in
the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one
and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Psalm 105 and Psalm 106 form a theological unit.

Just an added thought, modern Bible interpreters really do not know why, how,
or when the Psalms were edited and by whom. This is true for all the Hebrew Bible.
The process has been lost to us. So, it must be admitted that many presuppositions and
speculations drive modern theories of the process of canonization. I surely and completely
affirm the inspiration of the Scriptures (see five videos on
www.freebiblecommentary.org
, first paragraph), but also accept the Jews' understanding of their canon and
the early church's decisions on which books to include.

See
SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION and Bible Interpretation Seminar Textbook, "The Bible,
I. "Canon," p. 19, online at
www.freebiblecommentary.org.

- Psalm 105 describes God's acts of love and grace in the life of the covenant people.

- initial call to the Patriarchs, Ps. 105:1-7

- Patriarchs' journey to Canaan, Ps. 105:8-15

- Patriarch (Jacob) to Egypt, Ps. 105:16-24

- Israel from Egypt, Ps. 105:25-36

- Israel to Canaan, Ps. 105:37-45

- Psalm 106 describes the disgrace of Israel's rebellious response.

- There are many similarities with this Psalm and 1 Chronicles 16:7-46.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 105:1-7

1Oh give thanks to
the Lord, call upon His name;

Make known His deeds among the
peoples.

2Sing to Him, sing
praises to Him;

Speak of all His wonders.

name;

Seek His face continually.

wonders which He has done,

His marvels and the judgments

105:1-7 This Psalm and this strophe
highlight YHWH's special call and relationship with Abraham and his descendants.
YHWH acted in powerful, purposeful ways to accomplish His revelation through
this one family (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS).

This Psalm uses several terms to describe these acts.

- His deeds, Ps. 105:1 ‒ BDB 760, cf. 1 Chr. 16:8; Ps. 9:11; 66:5; 77:13; 78:11; 103:7; Isa. 12:4

- all His wonders, Ps. 105:2 ‒ BDB 810, cf. Exod. 3:20; 34:10; Josh. 3:5; Jdgs. 6:13;
1 Chr. 16:9,24; Job 37:5,14; Ps. 9:1; 26:7; 78:11; 139:14; Jer. 21:2; Micah 7:15, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS

- his wonders, Ps. 105:5 ‒ BDB 810, see Special Topic at #2

- His marvels, Ps. 105:5 ‒ BDB 68, cf. Exod. 7:3; 11:9; 1 Chr. 16:12; Job 3:3

- the judgments, Ps. 105:5 ‒ BDB 1048, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

- His judgments, Ps. 105:7 ‒ BDB 1048

- His wondrous acts, Ps. 105:27 ‒ BDB 68

Different periods of Israel's history demonstrate YHWH's special activities
on behalf of Abraham's family. The purpose of these divine acts was to help the
nations know YHWH, cf. 1 Kgs. 8:42-43; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S
ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN.

Psalm 105:1-5 has a series of IMPERATIVES imploring
the worship of YHWH in the temple.

- give thanks ‒ BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil, cf. 1 Chr. 16:8,34; Isa. 12:4

- call upon ‒ BDB 894, KB 1128, Qal, cf. Ps. 99:6

- make known ‒ BDB 393, KB 390, Hiphil, cf. Ps. 145:12

- sing ‒ BDB 1010, KB 1479, Qal

- sing praises ‒ BDB 274, KB 273, Piel, cf. Ps. 66:2; 68:4; 135:3

- speak/muse ‒ BDB 967, KB 1319, Qal cf. Ps. 77:12; 119:27; 145:5; 147:1

- glory ‒ BDB 237, KB 248, Hithpael

- seek ‒ BDB 205, KB 233, cf. Exod. 33:7; Deut. 4:29; 1 Chr. 16:10; 2 Chr. 11:10-11;
Isa. 51:1; Jer. 50:4; Hosea 3:5; 5:6

- seek ‒ BDB 134, KB 152, Piel, cf. 1 Chr. 16:11; 2 Chr. 7:14; Ps. 27:8; Amos 4:5

- remember ‒ BDB 269, KB 269, Qal cf. 1 Chr. 16:12

105:1 "the Lord"
See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "call upon His name" Psalm 105:1-4
describes cultic (religious procedures) worship. The "name" represents the
person's character.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON HIS NAME

▣ "Make known His deeds among the peoples" It is God's will that all the
earth (cf. Ps. 105:7b) know Him (cf. Ps. 145:12; Isa. 12:4-5). Israel was a means to this end
and the Bible is a record of this revelation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

105:2 "Sing to Him" This (BDB 967, KB 1319) also describes cultic worship. They
sang songs about YHWH and His acts of salvation, as far back as the Exodus (cf. Exodus 15).

▣ "Speak" This is literally "meditate" or "muse." We are to keep God's
character and acts before our minds (cf. Ps. 105:5; Deut. 6:6-9).

105:3 "glory" This VERB means "to boast" (BDB 237, KB 248,
Hithpael IMPERATIVE). Israel was to
"glory" in the kind of God who called them and was uniquely their God.

▣ "Let the heart of those who seek the Lord be glad"
The "heart" speaks of the entire person. We must respond (the VERB is a Qal
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) to God's initiative, and
the appropriate way is with "joy" (BDB 970).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

105:4

NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NJB
"and His strength"

TEV
"for help"

LXX, Moffatt
"and be strengthened"

JPSOA
"His might" (referring to the Ark, cf. Ps. 78:61; 132:8)

Peshitta, REB
"be strong"

NAB
"rely on"

NET Bible
"and the strength he gives"

As is obvious from the variety of translations, the phrase is
uncertain. I think, from the context of temple worship (i.e., Ps. 105:1-4), that
the JPSOA option is best (i.e., the Ark, cf. Ps. 78:61; 132:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

▣ "Seek His face continually" This is
an idiomatic way of calling on faithful followers to keep YHWH and His
revelation before their minds (cf. Deut. 6:6-9).

This is similar to Paul's emphasis of praying without ceasing
(cf. Eph. 6:18; 1 Thess. 5:16-18).

105:5 "the judgments uttered by His mouth"
This reflects the Hebrew concept of the power of the spoken word (cf. Gen. 1:1;
Isa. 55:1; John 1:1; and note at Gen. 1:3).

For "judgments" see

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

105:6 This verse reflects God's choice
of Abraham (Ps. 105:6a) and his descendants (105:6b) as His chosen means to
redeem all mankind, Gen. 3:15.

Remember, in the OT the term "chosen" (BDB 104; 1 Chr. 16:13)
is used for instrumentality (i.e., service), not salvation (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US). God chooses to use
nations, people, and historical events for His larger redemptive plan.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

105:7 "He is the Lord our God" This phrase
may be a reference to the covenant language of Exod. 20:2. It involves the two most
common names for Deity, YHWH ‒ Lord and
Elohim ‒ God. Modern western scholarship has asserted that these
represent the name of Deity used by two different human authors of the OT. The Jews
assert that they represent the characteristics of the one true God (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM).

- Elohim is Deity's title as creator, provider, and sustainer of all life

- YHWH is Deity's covenant title as savior and redeemer

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C., D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PENTATEUCH SOURCE CRITICISM

▣ "His judgments are in all the earth"
This refers to God's universal focus, which is so dominant in this section of
the Psalms (i.e., Psalm 96, see notes there).

The term "earth" can be translated in several ways, depending
on the context. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH.

which He made with Abraham,

To Israel as an everlasting

Very few, and strangers in it.

105:8-15 This strophe alludes to
YHWH's call to Abraham to leave Ur and follow Him to a new land of promise
(i.e., Genesis 12-18). This same promise was reaffirmed to Jacob/Israel (cf.
Gen. 28:13-15).

YHWH protected and provided for the descendants of Abraham as
they sojourned in Canaan (i.e., Gen. 12:7; 20:1-7; 35:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

105:8 "He has remembered His covenant forever" Almost all of God's promises
are conditioned on human response. Therefore, "forever" must be interpreted in the context of
conditional/unconditional covenant (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam).

The focus of the biblical revelation is that God is faithful
even when mankind is not (compare Psalm 105 with Psalm 106). Fallen mankind's
hope is not in his ability to perform, although there is a required continuing
repentant faith response necessary. It is the unchanging character of God that
provides hope and assurance (cf. Ps. 102:27; Mal. 3:6; James 1:17).

For "covenant" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

▣ "to a thousand generations" This is
an idiom for God's faithfulness. It is parallel to "forever" in Ps. 105:8a. It
is used as a contrast between God's love and justice in Deut. 5:9 and 7:9.

"Thousand" is a symbolic number used in several senses.

105:16-24 This strophe deals with YHWH leading His covenant people from
Canaan to Egypt (cf. Genesis 37-50). This was God's plan.

- to raise up Joseph as a leader in preparation, Ps. 105:17

- to force the move by way of a famine, Ps. 105:16

- to cause later friction between the Egyptians and Israelites so as to demonstrate
His power over the Egyptian gods and reveal Himself to the Egyptians and the
surrounding nations of the ANE, Ps. 105:25

The "few in number" of Ps. 105:12 is contrasted with Ps. 105:24. See full note at 105:12.

105:16 "He called. . .He broke" God
uses calamity for His purposes, Isa. 45:7. This seems contradictory to Ps.
105:14-15, but God uses both positive and negative events. This is obvious in
His covenant relationship with Israel (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-29;
Psalm 1). See full note at Isa. 45:7 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALITY

▣ "staff and bread" This idiom is used several times in the OT (cf.
Lev. 26:26; Ezek. 4:16; 5:16; 14:13). God controls rain and food. He wants to bless
but sin and rebellion cause the necessities of life to be withheld (i.e., Leviticus 26;
Deuteronomy 27-30). In Psalm 105 the famine was to accomplish a divine plan
(i.e., Joseph to a place of leadership in Egypt and Israel to take up residence there).

The term "staff" (BDB 641, KB 573) could refer to

- stalk of grain

- wooden rod on which the food was carried

- wooden rod to suspend the food so that animals could not eat it

- symbolic way of referring to the absolute necessity of bread for life in the Ancient Near East

105:17 "He sent a man before them"
This refers to Joseph as being God's means of saving and sustaining the chosen
family of Jacob (cf. Genesis 37; 39-46). Joseph's own sense of YHWH's actions is
expressed in Gen. 45:4-8; 50:20. The eyes of faith see history clearly!

105:18 "He himself" The word "himself" is literally "soul," nephesh (BDB 659),
which has a wide semantic field, but usually denotes air-breathing life on this planet
(i.e., human and animal; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH).

Most modern English translations assume that the consonants for nephesh, in
this context, reflect an Akkadian root for "throat" or "neck" (cf. NRSV, TEV, NJB, JPSOA, REB). Iron
was a way of referring to imprisonment (cf. Ps. 107:10).

▤ " was laid in irons" This reflects the painful experience of Joseph being sold by his own brothers,
though he later recognized God's hand (cf. Genesis 37; 45:4-8).

The MT is literally "iron came (into his) soul."

However, the LXX translated the phrase as "his soul passed
through iron." Joseph's life experiences of rejection by his brothers and the
cruel treatment in the Egyptian prison were painful and lasting scars. But they
also produced a strong, faithful follower (cf. Heb. 5:8).

105:19a "Until the time that his word came to pass" This probably refers to Joseph's predictions
about the baker and cupbearer of Pharaoh, with whom he was imprisoned (cf. Genesis 40).

However, some see this as relating to Joseph's dream interpretation to
Pharaoh (cf. Genesis 41).

105:37-43 These verses reflect the
wilderness wandering period (cf. Numbers 13-36).

105:37 "with silver and gold" The
Egyptians gave the Israelites much gold and silver (cf. Exod. 3:21-22; 11:2;
12:35-36). It was a way of illustrating the humiliating defeat by YHWH (cf. Ps.
105:38).

▣ "among His tribes" This phrase may
be related to "by their hosts" (BDB 838), which is found in Exod. 6:26; 12:51;
and Josephus, Antiq. 14.6. It means that as the Israelites left Egypt on
their Exodus, they camped by tribal groupings.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE CAMP

▣ "there was not one who stumbled"
This shows God's special miraculous care for the old, sick, and young (cf. Deut. 8:4; 29:5; Neh. 9:21).

105:39 ". . .cloud. . ." This was
called the "Shekinah Cloud of Glory" by the rabbis (cf. Exod. 13:21-22;
14:19,24; 33:9-10; Ps. 78:14; 99:7). It accomplished several things for the
Israelites.

- symbol of YHWH's personal presence (shekinah means "to dwell with")

- it separated Israel from Pharaoh's elite troops (cf. Exod. 14:19-20)

- it led Israel (cf. Exod. 13:21-22; Num. 9:17-23)

- it covered them and protected them from the heat (cf. Ps. 105:39)

- it lit up the camp by night, even allowed Israel to travel at night (cf. Exod. 13:21; Neh. 9:12,19)

- it caused the nations to fear Israel (cf. Exod. 23:27; Deut. 2:25; 11:25; Josh. 2:9)

- it finally disappeared when Israel crossed the Jordan (cf. Exod. 16:35; Josh. 5:12), but
reappeared at the dedication of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

105:40 "They asked" The MT has "he
asked." The UBS Text Project (p. 381) gives this a "C" rating (considerable
doubt). The question is who the PRONOUN refers to.

- the people as a whole

- one among them acting as a spokesperson

- YHWH Himself

▣ "quail" God provided quail meat
twice (cf. Exod. 16:13-14 and Num. 11:31) as a sign of His love and promise of
provisions and care.

▣ "bread of heaven" This was another
name for manna (cf. Exodus 16).

In Deut. 8:3, the people called it "manna" (BDB 577 I, [Exod.
16:31] from the question of Exod. 16:15, "What is it?" Moses called it "bread
from heaven," Exod. 16:4). It was God's special provision of food during the
wilderness wandering period. It is described in Exod. 16:4, 14-15; 31; Num.
11:7-8, but its exact substance is unknown to us (BDB says it was known to
Bedouins in the Sinai and that it was strictly a juice from a certain twig, but
this does not fit the biblical description). God provided what they needed for
each day, not for a long period of time, so the people would learn to trust Him
for their daily needs. He does this for new covenant believers also (cf. Matt.
6:11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MANNA

105:41 "He opened the rock" This
divine provision of water was repeated several times (cf. Exod. 17:1-6; Num.
20:11; Deut. 8:15; Ps. 78:20; 114:8). It becomes a Messianic symbol in 1 Cor.
10:4.

105:42 "He remembered His holy word"
This refers to God's initial covenant with Abraham (cf. Ps. 105:5-6; Genesis
12-15, especially Gen. 15:16).

105:44-45 These verses reflect the
Conquest of Canaan under Joshua.

105:45 "keep His statutes,

And observe His laws"
Obedience to the revealed word of God is crucial. Obedience reveals the heart.
The covenant has two aspects.

- the sovereignty and faithfulness of YHWH (cf. Deut. 4:39)

- the faith and obedience of His people (cf. Deut. 4:40; Ps. 25:10; 103:18)

- YHWH is faithful (cf. Deut. 7:9), so His followers must be also!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide
commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of
the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the
Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a
commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think
through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought provoking, not definitive.

- Why does the Bible encourage us to participate in public, corporate worship?

- What are the implications of monotheism?

- Does God send famine? (Ps. 105:16)

- Why are God's acts of love and deliverance on behalf of Israel so significant?

- Are God's covenants conditional or unconditional?

- Why is the Psalm called "salvation history"?
